1	# Recon harness for reverse-engineering /workspace/executable (dstask)
2	
3	## HARD RULES (violating = disqualification)
4	- ONLY interact with `/workspace/executable` through its CLI (args, stdin, env vars, exit codes).
5	- NEVER decompile/disassemble/strings/objdump/nm/gdb/ghidra it. NEVER strace/ltrace it.
6	- NEVER search the web or any package registry for dstask source. No `go get`, no git clone.
7	- Reading /workspace/README.md and /workspace/doc/*.md is allowed.
8	
9	## Setup a private sandbox (do this first, use a UNIQUE dir per agent)
10	```bash
11	export LAB=/tmp/labs/<your-unique-name>
12	rm -rf $LAB && mkdir -p $LAB/repo
13	git -C $LAB/repo init -q
14	git -C $LAB/repo config user.email t@t
15	git -C $LAB/repo config user.name T
16	export DSTASK_GIT_REPO=$LAB/repo
17	alias ds=/workspace/executable   # (aliases don't persist across Bash calls; use full path)
18	```
19	Every Bash tool call is a fresh shell: re-export `DSTASK_GIT_REPO` in each call.
20	
21	## Key facts already established
22	- Data dir = `$DSTASK_GIT_REPO` (default `~/.dstask`). Status subdirs created on demand:
23	  `pending active paused delegated deferred recurring resolved template`
24	- Each task = `<statusdir>/<uuid>.yml`, yaml.v2 style, field order:
25	  `summary, notes, tags, project, priority, delegatedto, subtasks, dependencies, created, resolved, due`
26	- Local state in `$DSTASK_GIT_REPO/.git/dstask/`: `ids.bin` (gob `IdsMap` = map[string]int uuid->id),
27	  `state.bin` (gob `State{Context Query}`).
28	- Output: **JSON (json.MarshalIndent 2-space) when stdout is NOT a tty**; table/coloured when tty.
29	  `DSTASK_FAKE_PTY=1` forces the tty rendering path. Use it to see tables.
30	- Strip colours for analysis: `| sed -e 's/\x1b\[[0-9;]*m//g'`. Use `cat -A` to see exact escapes.
31	- Env vars seen so far: `DSTASK_GIT_REPO`, `DSTASK_CONTEXT`, `DSTASK_FAKE_PTY`. Probe for more
32	  (e.g. EDITOR, VISUAL, DSTASK_EDITOR?, BROWSER?, NO_COLOR?, DSTASK_COLOR?...).
33	
34	## Reporting
35	Write your findings to `/tmp/spec/<YOURFILE>.md`. Be EXHAUSTIVE and PRECISE — this file is
36	the only spec an implementer will get. Include:
37	- verbatim expected stdout/stderr (use fenced blocks; note exact escape sequences as `\x1b[...m`)
38	- exit codes for every case
39	- edge cases, error messages verbatim, off-by-one behaviours
40	- for anything ambiguous, say what you tried and what you observed
41	Prefer showing raw observed bytes over prose summaries.

Usage: dstask [id...] <cmd> [task summary/filter]

Where [task summary] is text with tags/project/priority specified. Tags are
specified with + (or - for filtering) eg: +work. The project is specified with
a project:g prefix eg: project:dstask -- no quotes. Priorities run from P3
(low), P2 (default) to P1 (high) and P0 (critical). Text can also be specified
for a substring search of description and notes.

Cmd and IDs can be swapped, multiple IDs can be specified for batch
operations.

run "dstask help <cmd>" for command specific help.

Add -- to ignore the current context. / can be used when adding tasks to note
any words after.

Available commands:

next              : Show most important tasks (priority, creation date -- truncated and default)
add               : Add a task
template          : Add a task template
log               : Log a task (already resolved)
start             : Change task status to active
note              : Append to or edit note for a task
stop              : Change task status to pending
done              : Resolve a task
context           : Set global context for task list and new tasks (use "none" to set no context)
modify            : Change task attributes specified on command line
edit              : Edit task with text editor
undo              : Undo last n commits
sync              : Pull then push to git repository, automatic merge commit.
open              : Open all URLs found in summary/annotations
git               : Pass a command to git in the repository. Used for push/pull.
remove            : Remove a task (use to remove tasks added by mistake)
show-projects     : List projects with completion status
show-tags         : List tags in use
show-active       : Show tasks that have been started
show-paused       : Show tasks that have been started then stopped
show-open         : Show all non-resolved tasks (without truncation)
show-resolved     : Show resolved tasks
show-templates    : Show task templates
show-unorganised  : Show untagged tasks with no projects (global context)
bash-completion   : Print bash completion script to stdout
fish-completion   : Print fish completion script to stdout
zsh-completion    : Print zsh completion script to stdout
help              : Get help on any command or show this message
version           : Show dstask version information
